metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — force forecast to align with recent 3–5 day moving average.
- Model underestimates downward trends after spikes — if true outcome drops below 30-day low, adjust forecast to reflect at least 2–3 day lagged decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage volatility — add 1–2% downward adjustment for final 5–7 days if sentiment remains flat.
- If true outcome shows sudden reversal after a spike, model fails to anticipate — apply “reversal buffer” rule: if price drops >5% from peak, forecast must drop >3% in next 3 days.
